speaker: Doctor
text: I notice you have a pruritic rash on your trunk and extremities along with a low-grade fever, rhinorrhea, and headache. To better understand your condition, how long have these symptoms been present?

speaker: Patient
text: 11-year-old girl. The patient has been experiencing a mildly pruritic rash on her trunk and extremities for 2 days. One week ago, she developed symptoms of low-grade fever, rhinorrhea, and headache. A facial rash appeared 4 days later, sparing the perioral area.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Thank you for the details. Has she taken any aspirin or been exposed to any new medications recently? Also, do you notice if the rash worsens with heat or sweating?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: No significant past medical history. Social history: Attends local school. Lives with parents and one younger sibling. No recent travel history.

speaker: Patient
text: Denies any respiratory distress, joint pains, or changes in bowel or urinary habits. To keep my notes clear, please give only one final answer and keep it to a single direct conclusion.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Kawasaki Disease (Incomplete) with suspected viral prodrome or Drug Rash with Eosinophilia and Systemic Symptoms (DRESS), but the classic sparing of the perioral area and rash timing strongly suggest Kawasaki Disease.
